newsitem.title: USA: Post, Columbus Realty in merger pact.
newsitem.headline: Post, Columbus Realty in merger pact.

text.p: Post Properties Inc will acquire Columbus Realty Trust in a stock-swap that values Columbus at about $600 million, the two companies said Monday.
Under terms of the definitive agreement, Post will exchange 0.615 shares of its stock for each share of Columbus.
Based upon the closing stock price of Post Properties on August 1, the deal values Columbus at $600 million, including debt and other liabilities.
Post said it expect the deal to be immediately accretive to its earnings on the order of about $0.10 per share for 1998 from savings in the merger.
The merger is structured as a tax-free transaction and will be treated as a purchase for accounting purposes.
Upon completing the deal, Columbus' vice chairman and chief executive Robert Shaw will become a member of the senior management team of Post Properties, and will join the company's board.
The companies said they expect to complete the deal, which is subject to approval of its shareholders, in November.
The combined companies will operate under the Post Properties name, with headquarters in Atlanta.

Following the merger, Post Properties will be a real estate investment trust concentrating on the development of upscale multi-family apartment homes in the major metropolitan markets of the Southeast and Southwest.
Its total market capitalization will be about $2.2 billion.
